qwen3_32b.comparison: 100pt scale reduces tie rate from 72.7% to 51.1% (Δ=-21.6pp), but ATE remains non-significant (p=0.15). Qwen clusters at multiples of 5 (45,65,75,85), behaving as a ~20-point effective scale rather than true continuous.

llama_70b.comparison: 100pt scale reduces tie rate from 72.7% to 39.8% (Δ=-32.9pp), the largest reduction across all judges. Llama uses diverse non-round values (78,87,89,82), approximating continuous scoring better than Qwen or GPT-4o. ATE still non-significant (p=0.44). 5 pairs failed due to Llama returning score=0.

gpt4o_reference.note: GPT-4o 100pt results from existing experiment. GPT-4o clusters heavily at multiples of 25 (0,25,50,75,100), behaving as a 5-point effective scale.

cross_judge_summary.conclusion: Expanding Likert from 1-10 to 1-100 reduces tie rates for all judges but does not improve statistical power for detecting style bias (all p>0.15). Granularity varies by judge: GPT-4o collapses to 5 bins, Qwen to ~20 bins, Llama achieves the finest granularity. The ATE direction is inconsistent across judges (GPT-4o slightly negative, Qwen/Llama slightly positive), confirming formality style does not systematically bias quality judgments.
